text: As people, more people come on chain, they want to have access to more assets. And many of those have been enabled by R3 and what we now call RWA for previously known securitization and tokenization. And I think that's really, again, very ideal time for starting to converge the more traditional world, the institutional world, and then also the blockchain native world. And so what I think we can accomplish together is to finally enable regulated financial institutions that are already really interested in public blockchains. See, at the very least, this is about distribution of assets, enabling financial access for a much broader audience, both on the buy side and the sell side. And this is about enabling those regulated institutions to fully harness the openness and efficiency of public blockchains, and doing that in ways that also honor the needs when it comes to compliance, security, and asset control. So ultimately, look, when you think about financial markets enabling global financial markets access, the most important feature of any financial market is liquidity. That means both a diversity of counterparties and also liquidity in, of course, assets. And this is exactly what we've been focused on with Solana, which is why from the very beginning, we always thought about Solana as maximally being one unified environment. Engineers call that a single state machine. And if you translate that into the capital markets world, that means is unified liquidity. And I think that is what we can also bring as the value to R3's customer base, which is assets that have been issued on chain over the last 10 years and bringing them into this public marketplace as appropriate. Meet us at Internet Capital Markets.
